theme: SCE psychological attributes: public data feasibility, variables, respondent matching, access, and historical vintage
historical_cutoff_context: The key backward-looking B check is the 2021-05/06 SCE target period. Current files are not evidence of historical availability unless an official release record or archived byte-vintage supports it.

recommendation.within_sce_A: Retain verified same-respondent SCE fields as observed-state candidates. Q1 is retrospective current financial experience; Q2 is a near-target future financial outlook proxy and was not in the prior baseline. Neither is implicitly approved for P.
recommendation.external_donor_candidate: GSS 2018 HAPPY + SATFIN, optionally TRUST only after checking same-person and ballot complete-case support in the historical file. Official publication by 2019-03-19 is verified; 2018 row-level overlap and exact historical file vintage are not.
recommendation.fallback: SHED 2019 financial-experience items for a finance-state fallback if the historical public-use file is archived and same-respondent X support is audited. SHED is not a happiness/trust/trait-optimism source based on inspected 2024 codebook.
recommendation.not_eligible_for_2021_05_B: GSS 2021 was released after the target cutoff. Same-month SCE core microdata are released with a nine-month lag. SHED 2020 public-use first-release day is unresolved; do not assume eligibility.
recommendation.matching_warning: Cross-survey matching creates conditional synthetic donor distributions; it is not a one-to-one link between SCE residents and GSS/SHED respondents. GSS/SHED adult-person samples do not equal SCE household-head sample.

source_families.family: New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations (SCE) core microdata

local_existing_file.provenance_note: Already present in the pre-existing SCE audit manifest; not newly downloaded by this task. Current public file spans 2020-2024 and was retrieved in 2026, not a 2021 vintage.

source_families.population_and_unit: Monthly rotating internet panel of roughly 1,200-1,300 U.S. household heads; one row per respondent-month, with a stable panel user ID and month.
source_families.weights: Monthly SCE weight column `weight`; the required month-specific historical public vintage and publication date must be established before any B use.

fields_verified.meaning: Respondent/family current financial position versus 12 months earlier; ordinal 1 much worse through 5 much better.
fields_verified.role: retrospective self-reported state/experience; not happiness or objective financial stress

fields_verified.meaning: Expected respondent/family financial position 12 months ahead versus now; ordinal 1 much worse through 5 much better.
fields_verified.role: near-target future household-finance proxy; contemporaneous B input prohibited; a lagged value also needs publication-date evidence

fields_verified.meaning: Primary-residence housing tenure/ownership-status field; observed public categories 1-3, full label mapping not verified this turn.
Self-rated health: 1 excellent, 2 very good, 3 good, 4 fair, 5 poor.
Willingness to take financial risks; scale 1-7, endpoints not willing at all / very willing.
fields_verified.role: risk-tolerance proxy, not a general validated personality scale; only new respondents

fields_verified.meaning: General willingness to take risks in daily activities; scale 1-7.

fields_verified.field: QNUM1, QNUM2, QNUM3, QNUM5, QNUM6, QNUM8, QNUM9
fields_verified.meaning: Raw numeric responses to numeracy questions; codebook questionnaire says these questions are asked only of new respondents.
fields_verified.role: numeracy test items, not raw continuous latent score
derived all-row covariate; thresholds and across-wave derivation/update logic not verified

fields_verified.meaning: Ten-column public representation of Q10 employment situation; all columns exist and are nonmissing in the checked rows.
fields_verified.role: employment X; full value/label crosswalk not verified

source_families.joint_records: Same respondent-month row supports joining Q1/Q2, observed demographics, employment and new-entry questions when answered. Q1-Q2 complete rows are 1233 in 2021-05 and 1296 in 2021-06. New-entry fields are only about 12% of monthly rows; exact multi-field complete-case intersections were not computed.
source_families.release_and_access: Free official public data. NY Fed FAQ says SCE core and Credit Access microdata are released with a nine-month lag. This current downloaded file does not establish when each historical month first became public.
source_families.reading_status: Official SCE overview and FAQ reviewed; public questionnaire PDF inspected for Q1/Q2, Q45b, QRA1/QRA2 and new-respondent QNUM wording; actual two month slices from the pre-existing current XLSX read. No target association or Q8/Q9 analysis performed.
limitations: The current workbook is a revised later vintage and cannot establish 2021 B availability.
Q1 is self-reported retrospective change, not objective pressure; Q2 is target-proximate.
Numeracy, risk, health and Q43 are new-entry items, not all-panel fields; do not replace missingness with zero or a default.
_NUM_CAT is fully present but its derivation was not verified.

source_families.family: NORC General Social Survey (GSS), 2018 cross-section candidate
source_families.population_and_unit: National U.S. adult individual cross-section; unit is a respondent, not necessarily the SCE household head.

candidate_fields.meaning: Current overall happiness, three ordered response categories (very, pretty, not too happy).
candidate_fields.status: candidate for 2018; 2018 row distribution and ballot-specific missingness not computed

candidate_fields.meaning: Satisfaction with current respondent/family financial situation, three ordered response categories.
candidate_fields.status: candidate for 2018; exact 2018 joint support with HAPPY/TRUST/X not computed

candidate_fields.meaning: Interpersonal trust, most people can be trusted versus cannot be too careful.
candidate_fields.status: candidate for 2018; 2021 codebook explicitly says TRUST absent in 2021

candidate_fields.meaning: Single agreement item on whether respondent/family have a chance to improve their standard of living.
candidate_fields.status: found in 2021 codebook; 2018 availability not verified. Single item, not a validated trait-optimism scale.

candidate_fields.meaning: Whether financial situation has been getting better/worse/same over the last few years.
candidate_fields.status: retrospective in 2021 codebook; never label as future optimism

candidate_fields.meaning: Current family income relative to U.S. families generally.
candidate_fields.status: relative current status, not a future forecast

common_x_candidates: family income (check REALINC/original income field and harmonize to SCE household income bands)
source_families.x_gaps: No public state/CZ equivalence confirmed; household-head versus adult-person unit differs; income definition and education/employment/tenure category mappings need recoding and overlap validation.
source_families.weights: Current GSS FAQ recommends WTSSPS generally and WTSSNRPS for 2004-2024 nonresponse adjustment. These later post-stratification weights were created/released after 2018; strict B must use and archive the weight variable in the contemporaneous 2018 public release, not retroactively claim later weights were known.
source_families.historical_release: NORC official announcement dated 2019-03-19 verifies 2018 GSS results were publicly available before the 2021-05 cutoff. It does not verify that today's cumulative download is byte-identical to that 2019 release.
source_families.access: Free public use annual files in Stata/SAS/SPSS via NORC; GSS Data Explorer can make custom extracts. Official download ZIP and actual respondent microdata were not fetched this turn.
source_families.joint_support_status: NOT VERIFIED: 2018 HAPPY + SATFIN + TRUST complete-case respondent overlap and ballot assignment must be calculated from the historical 2018 file. Do not describe this as an accepted joint donor until audited.
source_families.reading_status: Official data/documentation pages, 2018 release announcement, 2018 questionnaire index and codebook listing reviewed. The large 1972-2018 cumulative codebook is distributed as an official ZIP; it was not extracted/read. No 2018 microdata were downloaded.
source_families.recommendation: Preferred external psychological donor candidate for both retrospective synthesis and potentially historical B only after historical-vintage and same-record support audit.

source_families.version: Codebook Release 4, produced 2024-11-25; official annual PUF release is later than 2021-05 cutoff.

fields_and_validity.HAPPY: 4,014/4,032 valid; current overall happiness, 1 very happy, 2 pretty happy, 3 not too happy.
fields_and_validity.SATFIN: 4,016/4,032 valid; current family financial satisfaction, 1 pretty well, 2 more or less, 3 not at all.
fields_and_validity.GOODLIFE: Single forward-looking living-standard opportunity agreement item appears in the codebook; not a multidimensional trait measure.
fields_and_validity.FINALTER: 4,021/4,032 valid; retrospective change over the last few years.
fields_and_validity.FINRELA: Current family income relative standing; not a future forecast.

source_families.joint_records: Variables occur in the same individual-level cross-section file; pairwise complete cases were not computed from microdata. Codebook shows marginal valid counts, not a row intersection audit.
source_families.mode_and_vintage: Pandemic-era 2021 collection used primarily web/self-administered mode, unlike historical face-to-face rounds. Its release follows the May 2021 SCE target cutoff, so it is not historical B input.
source_families.reading_status: Official 740-page codebook opened online; targeted fields, questionnaire text, valid counts and release/mode sections reviewed. File not downloaded; no respondent-level calculations.

source_families.family: Federal Reserve Board Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking (SHED)
source_families.population_and_unit: Annual U.S. adult respondent survey using address-based recruitment/probability-based online panel; respondent-level, not necessarily household head; excludes institutionalized adults and some adults without a physical address.
source_families.2024_codebook_version: 12,295 respondents; codebook last updated 2025-05-28; 2024 data last updated 2026-02-09. These current revisions are not available to 2021 B.

verified_fields.meaning: Current self-rated financial management: 1 difficult to get by, 2 just getting by, 3 doing okay, 4 living comfortably.
Effect of prices paid versus last year on household financial situation: 1 much worse, 2 somewhat worse, 3 little/no effect, 4 somewhat better, 5 much better.
Household monthly income / spending compared with a year earlier: decreased, about same, increased.

source_families.psychometric_gaps: Inspected codebook keyword searches found no `happy` or `optimistic` measure; no general interpersonal-trust scale was verified. B2/INF4 are financial state/experience, not happiness or dispositional optimism.
source_families.common_x_gaps: Employment status field mapping not verified; respondent person unit differs from SCE household head. Geography beyond public-use coarse categories is limited.
source_families.weights: Annual cross-section `weight` and population-total `weight_pop`; 2023-2024 panel sample uses `panel_weight` and `panel_weight_pop`.
source_families.historical_release: Official data page records 2019 public-use data/state field update dated 2021-05-07. 2020 SHED report was published 2021-05-17, but report date does not prove 2020 PUF release date; initial public-use release remains unverified. For a 2021-05-12 cutoff, only an archived 2019 file with its update record is currently a plausible SHED candidate.
source_families.access: Official free CSV/Stata ZIP data and public codebooks; ZIP data were not downloaded. No registration or restricted microdata requested.
source_families.reading_status: 2024 official codebook opened and targeted B2/INF4/I21/demographic/weight sections read; official data and FAQ pages reviewed. 2019/2020 microdata and historical snapshots not downloaded.

source_families.family: Special-panel candidates: HRS, MIDUS, and UAS (screened as one alternative-access family; not bulk downloaded)
source_families.HRS: Official 2018 early Core release announcement is 2019-12-18; 2018 psychosocial codebook has `QLB018B` future-optimism item. HRS primarily covers ages 50+ and partners, so it is a sensitivity source only, not a donor for all U.S. adults. Free data require account registration; early release is subject to later correction. Joint field coverage not audited.
source_families.MIDUS: Longitudinal adult cohort beginning in 1995-96 with well-being/optimism measures; not a contemporary repeated cross-section. Public data are routed through MIDUS/ICPSR. Exact joint X coverage and historical vintage not checked; no download.
source_families.UAS: U.S. internet panel with online study/codebook metadata; individual data files require account registration and signed User Data Agreement. Public immediate-download status and exact candidate field support not verified; no registration/download.
source_families.reading_status: Official project data/access pages and one HRS 2018 release/codebook were screened. No full data/codebook batches or individual files downloaded.

integrity_note: No new raw or public source files were written. The existing SCE file SHA is transcribed from docs/sce_source_manifest.json. Official web documentation was inspected online and is not claimed as a local archive.
